# Curation Requirements Quality Checklist: AI-First Vocabulary Curation

**Purpose**: Review whether Feature 003's specification and plan define a measurable, internally consistent AI-first curation process and safe promotion into deterministic Anki source data.
**Created**: 2026-10-03
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when a reviewer determines the criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the written requirements meet the criterion; it does not mean implementation is complete.

## AI Roles and Stage Separation

- [x] CHK001 Is AI's primary responsibility for candidate discovery, research, verification, classification, and future growth explicit, while routine entries remain eligible for acceptance without item-by-item human review? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [x] CHK002 Is the boundary between candidate generation and final acceptance explicit enough to forbid a generating pass from approving its own output? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK003 Are the required stages and their outputs distinct enough that missing linguistic comparison, evidence audit, independent verification, adversarial review, or duplicate review blocks acceptance? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003; Plan §Curation sequence]
- [x] CHK004 Is the independent verifier's permitted context defined so it cannot merely repeat the generator's rationale or preferred verdict? [Clarity, Plan §Curation sequence; Contract §Role sequence and isolation]
- [x] CHK005 Is adversarial review required to actively challenge semantic alignment, commonness, register, region, alternate meanings, and relation claims, with unresolved objections preventing acceptance? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009; Plan §Quality boundaries]
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements clear about when a material edit to a cue, answer, relation, or evidence invalidates earlier verification and challenge results? [Recovery, Plan §Curation sequence; Data Model §Stage result]

## Evidence Quality and Independence

- [x] CHK007 Is the ordinary acceptance threshold stated as at least two inspected, claim-relevant external signals rather than two model assertions or unvisited links? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK008 Is source independence defined by underlying publisher or corpus, so mirrors, copied pages, and multiple pages from one source cannot satisfy the two-signal gate? [Ambiguity, Research §Evidence standards and source limitations; Data Model §Evidence record]
- [x] CHK009 Do the requirements identify which meaning and usage claims each evidence item must support, instead of allowing an unrelated pair of citations to meet a count? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008; Data Model §Candidate and claim records]
- [x] CHK010 Is the distinction between word existence, comprehension, common use, and preferred everyday choice clear for both locales? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [x] CHK011 Is dictionary existence explicitly insufficient to establish everyday preference, especially for `different-common-word` claims? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006/FR-008]
- [x] CHK012 Are within-locale alternatives, aligned sense, comparable register, and relevant regional scope required when a national everyday preference is claimed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006; Contract §Gate rules]
- [x] CHK013 Are conflicting or inconclusive sources required to remain visible and to block acceptance until the conflict is resolved, even when the evidence count is met? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-009/FR-011]
- [x] CHK014 Are provenance fields sufficient to revisit a source's exact claim, query or location, access time, observed context, locale, register, and limitations? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016; Data Model §Evidence record]
- [x] CHK015 Is the requirement for false friends measurably stronger than the ordinary gate, covering each language's relevant meaning, the misleading contrast, and separate verifier/adversarial agreement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007]

## Decision Semantics and Conservative Gates

- [x] CHK016 Are `accepted`, `hold`, and `rejected` defined as mutually exclusive final batch outcomes with clear reasons and no silent default to acceptance? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011; Data Model §Decision and lifecycle]
- [x] CHK017 Are evidence gaps, unresolved disagreement, ambiguous cues, and unresolved overlap explicitly assigned to `hold` or `rejected` rather than accepted? [Coverage, Spec §FR-009/FR-011]
- [x] CHK018 Is model self-confidence expressly excluded as sufficient evidence or as an override of mechanical quality gates? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010; Plan §Quality boundaries]
- [x] CHK019 Are the conditions for rejecting a disproven or duplicate candidate distinguishable from conditions for holding an investigable candidate? [Clarity, Contract §Gate rules]
- [x] CHK020 Is the relationship between confidence rationale, independent stage agreement, evidence quality, source conflicts, and final disposition specified without pretending a numeric model score is calibrated? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010; Data Model §Decision and lifecycle]

## Concept Identity, Duplicates, and Cue Quality

- [x] CHK021 Are the four relation values defined by common usage for the same neutral concept, with false-friend semantics distinguished from ordinary form similarity? [Clarity, Spec §Relation Rules]
- [x] CHK022 Are English cues required to disambiguate senses concisely enough that the two answers cannot be correct for different meanings of the same English word? [Coverage, Spec §FR-013]
- [x] CHK023 Are deterministic exact, normalized-form, plural, and morphological overlap checks distinguished from AI-assisted semantic overlap judgments? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012; Plan §Curation sequence]
- [x] CHK024 Are cross-batch synonyms, alternate English labels, and earlier held/rejected proposals included in overlap requirements, with unresolved semantic overlap blocking new IDs? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012; Data Model §Overlap record]
- [x] CHK025 Are merge, reject, and explicit-distinction outcomes defined before permanent ID allocation, so accidental semantic duplicates cannot receive separate IDs? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012/FR-015]
- [x] CHK026 Are six-digit permanent ID assignment, non-reuse after removal, correction versus new-concept treatment, and legacy `000001` review specified consistently? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015; Plan §Curation sequence; Data Model §ID ledger]

## Batch Lifecycle, Resumability, and Provenance

- [x] CHK027 Are bounded topic batches, candidate limits, prompt-set versions, and repeatable role procedures specified without relying on an undocumented interactive chat session? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001; Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK028 Are provider/model settings centralized or otherwise governed by one documented configuration boundary, while each stage records the exact model/tool and prompt version used? [Gap, Plan §Source Code; Data Model §Stage result]
- [x] CHK029 Are malformed or incomplete structured AI responses given a defined failure outcome, with no silent prose-to-approved-data repair? [Edge Case, Contract §Failure behavior]
- [x] CHK030 Are interruption and resumption rules clear for partial AI/research runs, including which completed stage artifacts can be reused and which require rerun? [Recovery, Contract §Failure behavior; Data Model §Stage result]
- [x] CHK031 Is it explicit that open, failed, or partly researched batches cannot mutate canonical learner data or allocate permanent IDs? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011/FR-015; Contract §Failure behavior]
- [x] CHK032 Are export failure, rollback, and repeated-export requirements sufficient to prevent a mismatched TSV and ID ledger or duplicate ID allocation? [Recovery, Contract §Failure behavior; Data Model §ID ledger]
- [x] CHK033 Are intermediate AI outputs, source observations, conflicts, decisions, reasons, and timestamps inspectable for later reevaluation and process metrics? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016/FR-019]
- [x] CHK034 Does every batch report require reconcilable generated/accepted/held/rejected counts plus relation distribution, duplicates, investigation items, and verification failures, including a zero-acceptance batch? [Measurability, Spec §FR-017; Contract §Batch report contract]

## Learner Data, Build Boundary, and Compatibility

- [x] CHK035 Is promotion limited to accepted, fully gated candidates, while curation metadata remains separate from the inspectable learner TSV? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011/FR-014/FR-020]
- [x] CHK036 Is the network/AI boundary explicit for normal validation, `.apkg` generation, and release builds, so none can trigger live model calls or research? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020; Plan §Quality boundaries; Constitution §IX]
- [x] CHK037 Are source fields, required relation values, and false-friend contrast rules consistent across the spec, plan, data model, and learner-source contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014; Contract §Accepted source]
- [x] CHK038 Is false-friend contrast specified as back-only and evidence-backed without silently changing the established five Anki note fields, or is any proposed field change conditioned on proven old-to-new import compatibility? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021/FR-022; Plan §Compatibility assessment]
- [x] CHK039 Are permanent GUID derivation and deck/model identity requirements insulated from relation, contrast, provenance, prompt version, batch ID, and other curation metadata? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015/FR-022; Contract §Build projection]
- [x] CHK040 Are old-to-new deck update expectations and release-blocking compatibility evidence specified separately from source-level GUID tests, so package tests alone are not treated as proof of existing-collection updates? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-006; Plan §Compatibility assessment]

## Initial Corpus and Evaluation Limits

- [x] CHK041 Is the initial corpus target justified by bounded verification effort, with everyday category and relation variety specified but no rule that promotes weak entries to fill a quota? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018/SC-003; Research §Initial corpus target and verification effort]
- [x] CHK042 Are acceptance measures scoped to observable gate records, seeded failure cases, duplicate prevention, reporting, and card identity without implying that deterministic tests can prove the linguistic truth of every entry? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-001–SC-007; Plan §Verification and release gates]
